verdict.rationale: Workers itself documents background automation: cron jobs, durable Workflows that chain steps, retry failed tasks and persist state for weeks, Queues integration, and Agents SDK scheduling with agents that hibernate and wake on demand. These are first-party platform features for autonomous execution, not workarounds. A community report notes CPU-time limits (30s free, 15min paid) for long-running agent tasks, which is a caveat rather than a contradiction. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of cron trigger configuration and scheduling semantics, and independent hands-on corroboration of autonomous background runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Schedule cron jobs, run durable Workflows, and integrate with Queues
you can build applications that chain together multiple steps, automatically retry failed tasks, and persist state for minutes, hours, or even weeks - with no infrastructure to manage
Each agent has its own state, storage, and lifecycle — with built-in support for real-time communication, scheduling, AI model calls, MCP, workflows, and more.
Agents hibernate when idle and wake on demand.
